userStories.title: storiesJson bypass on POST /api/specs/generate — skip LLM if caller provides stories
userStories.description:
Modify `POST /api/specs/generate` in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` to accept an optional `storiesJson` field (`UserStory[]`) in the request body. When `storiesJson` is present and non-empty, skip all LLM calls and act as a pure persistence operation: validate the array, write the spec file to `forge/specs/pending/<slug>.json`, insert a `spec_versions` row, emit a `generate` WAL event, and return `{ id, path, storiesCount }`. When absent, the existing LLM generation path is completely unchanged.

Add an early-exit branch at the top of the handler: `if (req.body.storiesJson) { /* validate + persist */ return res.status(201).json(...) }`. Everything below is untouched.

Validation when `storiesJson` is provided:
- `title` required on request body (becomes slug)
- `storiesJson` must be non-empty array
- Each story must have `id` (matching `/^[A-Z]+-\d{3}$/`), `title`, `description`, `acceptanceCriteria` (non-empty array)
- No duplicate story IDs (use a Set)
- `dependsOn` references must resolve to IDs within the same array
- Return 400 `ValidationError` on any violation

Spec path: `path.join(workspace.path, 'forge/specs/pending', slug + '.json')`. Create parent dir if missing (`fs.mkdir recursive`). WAL insert uses `ts` column not `created_at`. `generatedAt` set server-side to `new Date().toISOString()`. Update the `@swagger` JSDoc block to document the new optional `storiesJson` body field.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/generate with { title, storiesJson: [...] } returns 201 with { id, path, storiesCount } and file exists at workspace.path/forge/specs/pending/<slug>.json — no LLM call made
POST /api/specs/generate without storiesJson behaves identically to before
A wal_events row with event_type='generate' is inserted on successful storiesJson persist (uses ts column)
Submitting storiesJson with duplicate story IDs returns 400 ValidationError
Submitting storiesJson with a dependsOn reference to a non-existent story ID returns 400 ValidationError

userStories.title: Extend rorca_generate_spec MCP tool with optional stories param — skip LLM if provided
userStories.description:
Update `rorca_generate_spec` in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` to accept an optional `stories` param (`object[]`). When `stories` is provided, call `POST /api/specs/generate` with `storiesJson` set to the stories array (the bypass path built in US-002) instead of the LLM generation path. When absent, behaviour is unchanged.

Also update the tool's description to document the hybrid generation workflow:
> Before calling this tool, call `rorca_recall_workspace(query=<brief>)` to load historical semantic context (CAG → RAG → Knowledge Graph). Generate your stories in-session using that context plus your live codebase reads, then pass them here via the `stories` param to persist without a second server-side LLM call.

Input schema additions:
- `stories`: optional array of story objects — when provided, bypasses server-side LLM
- Keep all existing params (`workspaceId`, `title`, `brief`, `model`, `templateId`) unchanged
acceptanceCriteria: rorca_generate_spec called with stories=[...] POSTs to /api/specs/generate with storiesJson and returns the persisted spec id without making any LLM call
rorca_generate_spec called without stories behaves identically to before (server-side LLM generation path unchanged)
Tool description documents the hybrid workflow: recall first, generate in-session, submit via stories param

userStories.title: Rewire rorca_forge_and_run prompt to enforce hybrid context pipeline
userStories.description:
Update the prompt definition for `rorca_forge_and_run` in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` to enforce the new hybrid generation workflow.

The current prompt instructs the agent to call `rorca_generate_spec` with a brief and wait for server-side LLM generation. Replace this with the 3-step hybrid pipeline:

1. Call `rorca_recall_workspace(query=<brief>, titlesOnly=false)` to load historical semantic context — direction stack, CAG/RAG-ranked memories, knowledge graph file-touch history, recent runs, skills
2. Read relevant files from the codebase (glob/grep/read) to get live structural context
3. Generate stories in-session combining both sources, then call `rorca_generate_spec(stories=[...])` to persist without a second server LLM call

The prompt text should make explicit:
- `rorca_recall_workspace` with `query` set to the brief is REQUIRED before generation — without it, the spec will miss historical context (past story blast radius, known gotchas, convention drift)
- `titlesOnly=true` is available for a fast index pass before loading full context
- Stories submitted via `rorca_generate_spec(stories=[...])` skip server LLM entirely
- The server-side LLM path (no `stories` param) remains available as fallback for non-MCP browser UI clients
acceptanceCriteria: The rorca_forge_and_run prompt text includes an explicit instruction to call rorca_recall_workspace(query=<brief>) before generating stories
The prompt documents the 3-step pipeline: recall → in-session generation → rorca_generate_spec(stories=[...])
The prompt mentions that titlesOnly=true is available on rorca_recall_workspace for a lightweight index pass
The prompt preserves the existing approve+run steps after spec creation

userStories.title: storiesJson bypass on POST /api/specs/:id/add-stories and rorca_add_stories MCP tool
userStories.description:
Apply the same storiesJson bypass pattern to `POST /api/specs/:id/add-stories` in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts`. When `storiesJson` is provided in the request body, skip LLM generation and directly append the provided stories to the existing spec JSON, write back to disk, insert a `spec_versions` row, and return `{ id, addedCount, totalStories }`.

Also update `rorca_add_stories` in `backend/src/mcp/server.ts` to accept an optional `stories` param and pass it as `storiesJson` when present. Update the tool description to match the hybrid workflow documented in US-004.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:id/add-stories with storiesJson=[...] appends stories to the spec file without any LLM call and returns { id, addedCount, totalStories }
POST /api/specs/:id/add-stories without storiesJson behaves identically to before
rorca_add_stories called with stories=[...] uses the bypass path
Duplicate story IDs (against existing stories in the spec) return 400 ValidationError
